The only one of the Alien and Sedition Acts still in force. During a declared war, or an invasion or predatory incursion by a foreign nation or government, the President may detain, restrict, and remove nationals of the hostile country.

## Key provisions

- Trigger: a declared war, or an invasion or predatory incursion perpetrated, attempted, or threatened by a foreign nation or government.
- Applies to natives, citizens, denizens, or subjects of the hostile nation aged fourteen and older who are not naturalized.
- The President sets the terms by proclamation; courts may hear whether a person falls within the act.

## Why it matters

Used in the War of 1812 and both world wars, it is the oldest wartime authority in Title 50 and the counterpart for persons of what the [Trading with the Enemy Act](twea-1917.qmd) does for property. The dispute since 2025 is whether its triggers can be met without one of the [Declarations of War](declarations-of-war.qmd) and by a non-state group.

## Current status

In force. A March 2025 proclamation invoked it against alleged members of a Venezuelan gang, its first use outside a declared war. The Supreme Court required notice and a chance to seek habeas review and later blocked removals of the plaintiffs. A Fifth Circuit panel found the invocation unlawful in September 2025; that opinion was vacated, and in August 2026 the full court dismissed the case as moot without ruling on the question. Check current status.
